# dsh-plugin-web-focus

Focused reading for DSH (DeepSeek Harness):
`web_focus` fetches one URL and injects **the sentences

that answer a focus you
write**, instead of the whole page.

The built-in `web_fetch` injects a page's markdown as-is (up to the host's
output cap). This plugin

registers a separate tool, `web_focus`, that ranks
sentences by token overlap with `focus`, guarante

es coverage of rare query terms,
drops navigation chrome and compresses links, keeps the uncompresse

d original on
disk, and labels exactly how much was omitted.

**0.2.0 registers no fetch provider.** `web_fetch` keeps its stock behaviour; the
plugin reaches the

network only through the public `ctx.web.fetch()` API. There is
no `fetchProvider` patch and disabl
ing the bundle cannot break `web_fetch`.
## What changed in 0.2.2 (2026-10-18)

- A focused digest admits only headings that contain a focus term (at most 8);
unmatched headings ar

e skipped by both the forced set and the score fill. The
zero-match fallback still returns the page

outline. On the San Francisco check
this removed the 19 heading lines; the digest is now 17 non-omit

ted lines with
0 headings (2 navigation links and 4 citation/footer lines remain).
- `SANITIZE_CALL_

SITES` points at `assemble.js`'s `compressStage`; the stale
`provider.js` reference is removed.
## What changed in 0.2.1 (2026-10-18)

- Every content-bearing focus term now keeps its best sentence, not only terms
below a rarity thresh

old. `population` no longer loses to rarer words.
- The strongest query-bearing body sentences are p

rotected from coverage and
reconciliation, and long pages force at most 20 headings (0.2.2 narrows t

his to
focus-matched headings).
- `founding` / `foundation` now trigger the founding-date pass along

side
`founded` / `established` / `incorporated`.
- The live-page check below states the exact focus

`founded` / `established` / `incorporated`.
- The live-page check below states the exact focus used.
## What changed in 0.2.0 (2026-10-18)

The unreleased 0.1.0 prototype took over the fetch path and, when a digest
retained under 40% of a p

age's sentences, **injected the whole compressed page
instead**. A controlled benchmark (below) meas

injected the whole compressed page
instead**. A controlled benchmark (below) measured what that did:
| Page size | 0.1.0: injected | 0.2.x: injected | 0.1.0: key sentences kept | 0.2.x |

ll text) | 4.0k | 100% (by accident) | **100%** |
| 100k | 79.8k (capped full text) | 4.3k | 61% | *

*100%** |
| 200k | 79.8k (capped full text) | 4.4k | 56% | **100%** |
| no matching content | 30k /
Live-page checks, same code path (measured during development):

- `en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco`: 459,687 raw chars → 3,765 body chars
(0.8% of the raw page)

with focus `population mayor mission founding date`.
Population `873,965`, mayor `Daniel Lurie`, an

d `June 29, 1776` are all
present. The old full-text fallback produced 79.8k chars on this page.
- `

zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiamen`: 335,038 raw chars → 3,946 body chars (1.2% of
the raw page). The Simi
ng district and Hubin North Road 61 are present.
Four changes produced that:

1. **Query-term coverage.** Every content-bearing focus term keeps its
best-scoring sentence, not on

ly terms that pass a rarity threshold; rare
terms keep every occurrence or their two best sentences.

Coverage runs after
the score fill and may displace ordinary filler, never a protected answer.
Two

role/date fact passes cover shapes that share no query token: a
`| Mayor | Daniel Lurie |` row (role

+ person) and a `| Mission | June 29,
1776 |` row (earliest dated founding/incorporation row). The

date pass
recognises `founded`, `founding`, `foundation`, `established` and
`incorporated`.
2. **Spa

rse digest instead of the full-text breaker.** A low retention ratio now
yields a small digest plus

an explicit `⚠️ [digest: sparse match …]` note.
`full=true` (or the retained raw text) remains the w

ay to read everything.
Zero-match pages now return headings and first/last sentences — not 80k chars

of unrelated text.
[该节后续省略]
## How selection works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Scoring is in-page IDF × query-token overlap, plus small priors for position,
numbers and headings.

`focus` is a **keyword query**, not a summarization
instruction: write the words you expect the answ

*keyword query**, not a summarization
instruction: write the words you expect the answer to contain.
## Known boundary: paraphrase

Token-overlap selection cannot find a fact that shares **no vocabulary** with the
focus. The benchma

rk's paraphrase case (page says "closed a $42 million financing
round", focus says "how much outside

money did it take") keeps 2 of 3 key
sentences; the missing one has a score of 0.8 (numeric prior o

nly). This is a
limitation of lexical retrieval, not a tuning bug. Mitigations: write the focus
with

likely page vocabulary, use `full=true` for paraphrase-heavy pages, or read
the retained raw text.

The other adversarial cases — multi-sentence answers,
tables, Chinese pages, a rare term appearing i

n seven sentences, a key past the
80k cap — all keep 100% of key sentences.
## Requirements

- DSH with the built-in `web` service (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`).
- Node.js ≥ 18.
- `@deepseek-ai/
schemastery` (peer dependency; DSH provides it).
### Host fetch cap (important on long pages)

The host's http fetcher truncates decoded bodies at **100,000 chars** by default.
On a large Wikiped

ia page that cut lands inside the infobox, before the prose:
[该节后续省略]
## Security posture

- **It does not fetch anything itself.** Every request goes through
`ctx.web.fetch`, so URL validati

on, SSRF blocking, redirect policy, size caps and
charset rules remain the host's.
- **A security bl

ock is never disguised as success.** Host errors are propagated
unchanged; only this plugin's own po

st-processing failures fall back to the
page unprocessed (capped).
- **Fetched pages are untrusted d

ata.** They are sanitized before injection and
are never treated as instructions. See SECURITY.md fo

r the
reporting process.
